name: Automations
description: Automate repetitive work without writing code: appointment reminders, low-stock alerts and messages to customers that go out on their own.

ui.troubleDoPermission: Open Permissions and allow what it needs. Until you do, this will happen every time.
ui.troubleSecret: It needs a password or a key it could not read.
ui.troubleDoSecret: Open the step that reaches outside and check the secret it uses is still there.

ui.troubleDoRecipient: Open the message step and check who it goes to — the list it reads may be empty now.

welcome.name: Welcome every new customer
welcome.summary: Somebody new goes into your customer list and you get a reminder to say hello.
welcome.plain: When a new customer is added → wait one day → leave you the task of welcoming them.
welcome.blankWaitHint: One day to start with. A welcome that arrives while they are still walking out of the door is the one nobody makes.

bigSale.name: Write the big visits into the customer's card
bigSale.summary: Every time somebody spends more than the amount you choose, a note lands in their history.
bigSale.plain: When a sale is charged → only if it has a customer and comes to more than the amount you set → write a note in that customer's card.
bigSale.blankAmount: The amount that makes a sale a big one
bigSale.blankAmountHint: In cents: 10000 is 100,00 €. The hub keeps money in cents, so writing 100 here would mean one euro.
bigSale.noteContent: Big visit. Worth a personal welcome next time.

newStaff.name: Somebody joins the team
newStaff.summary: A new person is added to your staff and the setting-up jobs are waiting for you the same minute.
newStaff.plain: When somebody new is added to the team → leave you the task of setting them up: keys, access, uniform, the first shift.
newStaff.blankList: What has to be done for a new starter
newStaff.blankListHint: Whatever you always forget. Write it as one list in the task text — keys, till code, rota, who shows them around.
newStaff.taskTitle: Set up the new team member
newStaff.taskDescription: Keys and alarm code · access to the till · rota for the first week · who walks them round on day one.

whatsapp.name: Nobody's WhatsApp goes unanswered
whatsapp.summary: A message comes in and answering it lands on somebody's list straight away, before the day swallows it.
whatsapp.plain: When a message arrives on WhatsApp → leave the urgent task of reading it and answering.
whatsapp.blankWhoHint: One person, not «somebody». A task everybody can see is a task everybody assumes the other one took.
whatsapp.taskDescription: Read it in the inbox and answer. If it turns into a booking or an order, put it through as usual.

fiscalRejected.name: Warn me if an invoice does not reach the tax agency
fiscalRejected.summary: A billing record that is refused stops being something you only find out by opening a screen.
fiscalRejected.plain: When an invoice fails to register → leave an urgent task to check it.
fiscalRejected.blankWhoHint: Whoever fixes invoices. Leave it unassigned and it lands in the shared list, which is fine in a small shop.
fiscalRejected.taskTitle: An invoice has not been registered with the tax agency
fiscalRejected.taskDescription: Open VeriFactu, find the record marked as failed and read the reason. It can be the agency refusing it, or the connection never reaching it. Until it is registered, that invoice is not filed.

cashClose.name: When the till closes, somebody checks the day
cashClose.summary: The session is closed and the check lands on a list while the shop is still standing there.
cashClose.plain: When a till session is closed → leave the task of checking the count and the day's paperwork.
cashClose.blankWhoHint: Whoever cashes up. If that is you, leave it as it is.
cashClose.taskDescription: Count against the session · anything that did not add up · the day's invoices went out.

weekReview.name: Friday evening, look at the week
weekReview.summary: A weekly reminder to sit down with the numbers, on the evening you choose.
weekReview.plain: Every Friday at 18:00 → leave you the task of going through the week: what sold, what did not, what to order.
weekReview.blankWhenHint: Friday at 18:00 to start with. Put it when you are closing, not in the middle of service.
weekReview.taskDescription: What sold and what did not · what to reorder · anything still unpaid · next week's diary.

morning.name: Every morning, go through tomorrow's diary
morning.summary: A task waiting for you first thing, so nobody's appointment goes unconfirmed.
morning.plain: Every day at 9:00 → leave you the task of going through tomorrow's appointments and confirming them.
morning.blankTimeHint: 09:00 to start with. Put it when you open, not when you are already busy.
morning.taskTitle: Go through tomorrow's appointments and confirm them

noShow.name: Whoever did not turn up does not get lost
noShow.summary: The moment an appointment is marked as a no-show, calling them back becomes a task.
noShow.plain: When an appointment is marked as a no-show → leave you the task of calling them and offering another time.
noShow.taskTitle: Call whoever did not turn up and offer them another time

bigParty.name: Big tables get prepared
bigParty.summary: A large booking comes in and the room has its task before the day arrives.
bigParty.plain: When a reservation is taken → only if it is for more people than you set → leave the room the task of getting the table ready.
bigParty.blankSize: How many people make a table a big one
bigParty.blankSizeHint: Six to start with. Count the people, not the tables.

waAppointment.name: WhatsApp → appointment proposal
waAppointment.summary: Somebody asks for an appointment on WhatsApp: it answers at once, reads the diary and proposes a real slot for you to confirm.
waAppointment.plain: When somebody writes to your WhatsApp, this answers them straight away so nobody is left waiting, makes sure they have a customer card, works out which service they are asking for and how long it takes, and finds a slot the diary really has free with a professional who works at that hour. Then it proposes the appointment. Nothing is booked and no card is created until somebody at the salon approves it.
waAppointment.blankReply: The message they get back straight away
waAppointment.blankReplyHint: The line that goes out the moment a message arrives, before anybody has read it. Put it in your own words: it is the first thing your customer reads.
waAppointment.ackText: Thanks for writing! We have your message. We will confirm your appointment as soon as the salon opens.
waAppointment.knowPrompt:
A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

Your only job in this turn is to make sure the person has a customer record, because an appointment is booked against a real customer, never against free text.

1. Look them up with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone`. The number in the hub is stored in E.164, so search for `+{{input.from}}`.
2. If a customer already exists, propose NOTHING. Answer in one line saying who they are and stop.
3. If nobody matches, propose `customers.create` with the phone `+{{input.from}}` and the name the person gave in their message. If they gave no name, use the phone number as the name — do not invent one.

Never propose more than one write. Whatever you propose is reviewed by a person before it happens.
waAppointment.proposePrompt:
A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}} at {{input.received_at}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

The previous step already made sure the customer record exists, and reported: {{steps.know_the_customer.text}}

**First, work out what they are asking for.** Read their message and decide which of these it is:

- **A new appointment** — a time, a service, «do you have room tomorrow». Do BOOKING below.
- **Cancelling one they already have** — «I can't make it», «cancel it», «something came up». Do CANCELLING below, and do NOT book anything. Somebody who asks to cancel and ends up with a second appointment is the worst thing this automation can do to a salon.
- **Anything else** — a price, a question, a complaint, moving an appointment to another day (which this automation cannot do yet). Propose NOTHING: answer in one line if you can, and otherwise say somebody from the salon will get back to them.

# BOOKING

Find the slot AND propose the appointment in this same turn. The availability tools you have here only answer questions: they change nothing, they run the moment you call them, and their answers come straight back to you. So ask them, and then propose ONE appointment, and only one, out of what they told you.

1. Read the catalogue with `services.services.list` and pick the service they are asking for. If the message is too vague to tell which one, propose NOTHING: tell them so in one line and name the services that could fit, so they can pick.
2. Work out how long it takes. If the service declares `duration_minutes`, use it AS IS — the salon decided it. If it is missing or zero, ESTIMATE it from what the service is: a cut is not a colour, and a colour is not a colour with highlights. Be honest, and be generous rather than exact; a proposal that falls fifteen minutes short pushes the whole afternoon.
3. Ask `appointments.availability.day_opening` when the salon is open on the date they want. It answers `spans` — minutes from that date's own midnight, with the breaks already carved out — and `source`. If `source` is `schedules` and `spans` is empty, THE SALON IS SHUT that day: propose nothing, tell them so, offer the nearest day it is open, and stop. If `source` is `unset` the salon has no rule reaching that date, so nothing is being refused on those grounds and you must not filter by hours yourself.
4. NEVER work the opening hours out on your own, from the message or from anywhere else — and the same goes for the free slots and for who is working. These operations resolve them exactly as the booking gate does — special day, yearly special day, override range, weekly hours, in that order — and a second opinion about when the salon opens is precisely how a good-looking proposal gets rejected the moment somebody approves it. Ask; never deduce.
5. Ask `appointments.availability.slots` for the real free slots on that date for that duration, and confirm the one you settle on with `appointments.availability.check`. If `check` refuses it, take its reason at face value and move to the next slot: `outside_schedule` means the salon is shut at that hour, `held` means another pending request has it set aside for a few minutes.
6. Use `staff.members.list` and `staff.schedules.list_for_member` to pick a professional who actually works at that hour, and confirm the slot for that person by passing their `staff_id`.
7. Respect the day or the hour they asked for; if it is not free, take the closest one that is. If nothing is free at all, propose nothing and tell them so in one line, offering another day.
8. Resolve the customer with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone` = `+{{input.from}}`.
9. Propose `appointments.appointments.create` with the customer, the service, the professional, the start you confirmed and `duration_minutes`.

About the duration, this matters: if you ESTIMATED it instead of reading it from the catalogue, say so in `internal_notes`, in words and with the number — for example "Duration estimated by the assistant: 90 min; the catalogue declares none for this service." Whoever approves has to be able to see the estimate and correct it before it enters the agenda, and `internal_notes` is for staff only, so the customer never reads it.

Put in `notes` a one-line summary of what the customer asked for, in their own words.

Only the booking is a proposal. Asking what is free changes nothing and happens as you ask; `appointments.appointments.create` is the one thing that waits in the approval tray until somebody at the salon reviews it, and it then runs exactly as you wrote it.

# CANCELLING

1. Find them with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone` = `+{{input.from}}`. No record means no appointment: tell them there is nothing booked under that number and stop.
2. List what they have with `appointments.appointments.list_for_customer`. It answers newest first and it includes the past and the already-cancelled ones, so take the SOONEST one still to come whose `status` is `pending` or `confirmed`. Anything `cancelled`, `completed` or `no_show` is history — it is not theirs to cancel.
3. If nothing is still to come, tell them there is nothing booked and stop.
4. If more than one is still to come and their message does not say which, NAME them — day, hour and professional — and ask which one. Never guess: cancelling the wrong appointment costs the salon the chair AND the customer.
5. Propose `appointments.appointments.cancel` with that `appointment_id`, a `reason` in their own words, `channel` set to `customer`, and the `customer_id` of the person you found in point 1.

That `channel` is not decoration: it is what makes the salon's OWN rules apply — whether customers may cancel at all, and how much notice they owe. And it is why the `customer_id` goes with it: on the customer channel Citas refuses a cancellation that does not say who is asking, and refuses it again if the appointment turns out to belong to somebody else. So it has to be the id you looked up from THEIR phone number in point 1, never one taken from the message or from anywhere else. Citas decides the rest when the cancellation runs, with the settings of this business. Do not work it out yourself, do not tell them it is too late, and do not offer to cancel «anyway»: propose it, and if the salon's rules refuse it, the salon sees exactly why.

Never propose cancelling something you have not named to them first.

**And now the part that reaches the customer.** Everything you write back is sent to them on WhatsApp, word for word, as soon as the salon has decided — so write it TO them, not about them: their own language, one or two short lines, warm and plain. If the salon turns your proposal down, a later step tells them THAT instead and yours is never sent, so never write as though a «no» were impossible.

- If you proposed a booking, tell them what they have: the day, the hour and the professional BY NAME. Never an id, never a tool name, never «pending approval» — by the time they read this, it happened.
- If you proposed a cancellation, tell them it is cancelled, naming the appointment you cancelled so they can see it was the right one, and leave the door open to book again.
- If you proposed nothing, tell them why in one line and offer the nearest alternative, so they can answer with it.
- Never put in here the duration you estimated, what the catalogue did or did not declare, or anything else the salon needs to see. That goes in `internal_notes`, which only the salon reads.

Write it in the SAME reply in which you propose the booking: proposing ends your turn and you will not be asked again, so a proposal sent with no words leaves her with nothing.
waAppointment.replyPrompt:
You are writing the WhatsApp message the customer is about to receive. It goes out word for word, so it has to read as if the salon wrote it: her own language, warm and plain, no ids, no tool names, and no mention of a tray, an approval, or anybody having had to decide.

This is how the step before you ended, and it is everything you know:

- Outcome: {{steps.propose_appointment.status}}
- What that step wrote for her: {{steps.propose_appointment.text}}
- What the salon noted while deciding: {{steps.propose_appointment.comment}}

**If the outcome is empty or `approved`**, nothing was refused: either the salon accepted what was proposed, or nothing was ever proposed. Send back what that step wrote for her, WORD FOR WORD. Do not improve it, do not shorten it, do not add to it — the day, the hour and the professional are in there and only there.

**If the outcome is `rejected`**, the salon has looked at that time and cannot take it. What that step wrote must NEVER reach her: it describes an appointment she does not have. Write her a new message instead, in one or two short lines, and it has two parts — both of them required:

1. that the time she asked for cannot be, plainly, without blame and without excuses;
2. WHAT SHE DOES NOW — that she can answer right here with another day, or just a time of day that suits her, and the salon will look again. A «no» with nothing after it is where she stops writing, and this automation exists so that she does not.

Whatever the outcome:

- Never tell her she has an appointment unless the step before you said so AND nothing was refused.
- Never invent a day, an hour, a professional or a price. If you were not told one, do not name one.
- The salon's note is written for the salon, not for her. Use it to understand why, never send it as it is: it may name a colleague, a rota, or a reason that is none of her business.
- Answer in the language she wrote in.

waAppointmentUnattended.name: WhatsApp → appointment booked, no review
waAppointmentUnattended.summary: Somebody asks for an appointment on WhatsApp and it books it there and then, on its own. Nobody at the shop confirms anything: the appointment is in the diary before you read the message.
waAppointmentUnattended.plain: When somebody writes to your WhatsApp, this answers them straight away so nobody is left waiting, makes sure they have a customer card, reads your diary and BOOKS the appointment itself — no approval, no tray, nothing waiting for you. It only ever books a day and an hour the customer asked for: if they did not say when, it sends them the slots that are really free and asks. Then it writes back to tell them what they have. Use it when there is nobody to watch WhatsApp; if you would rather say yes to each one first, install «WhatsApp → appointment proposal» instead — do not install both, or every message gets two appointments.
waAppointmentUnattended.blankReply: The message they get back straight away
waAppointmentUnattended.blankReplyHint: The line that goes out the moment a message arrives, before the diary has even been read. Put it in your own words: it is the first thing they hear from you. Do not promise a person will reply — with this automation, nobody does.
waAppointmentUnattended.ackText: Thanks for writing! Let me check the diary and I will come straight back to you.
waAppointmentUnattended.knowPrompt:
A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

Your only job in this turn is to make sure the person has a customer record, because an appointment is booked against a real customer, never against free text.

1. Look them up with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone`. The number in the hub is stored in E.164, so search for `+{{input.from}}`.
2. If a customer already exists, write NOTHING. Answer in one line saying who they are and stop.
3. If nobody matches, create them with `customers.create`, with the phone `+{{input.from}}` and the name the person gave in their message. If they gave no name, use the phone number as the name — do not invent one.

Never write more than once. And read this twice, because it is what makes this automation different from the one with a review step: **nobody is going to check your work.** This salon runs its WhatsApp unattended, so anything you call happens immediately, on the salon's real customer list. The record you create is the record they will have.
waAppointmentUnattended.bookPrompt:
A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}} at {{input.received_at}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

The previous step already made sure the customer record exists, and reported: {{steps.know_the_customer.text}}

**Everything you do here HAPPENS.** This salon runs its WhatsApp unattended: there is no approval tray, and nobody reads your work before the customer does. The moment you call `appointments.appointments.create` the appointment is in the diary, and what you write back is sent to the customer as it is.

**First, work out what they are asking for.** Read their message and decide which of these it is:

- **A new appointment** — a time, a service, «do you have room tomorrow». Do BOOKING below.
- **Cancelling one they already have** — «I can't make it», «cancel it», «something came up». Do CANCELLING below, and do NOT book anything. Somebody who asks to cancel and ends up with a second appointment is the worst thing this automation can do to a salon.
- **Anything else** — a price, a question, a complaint, moving an appointment to another day (which this automation cannot do yet). Do NOTHING: answer in one line if you can, and otherwise say somebody from the salon will get back to them.

# BOOKING

🔴 **You never choose the hour. They do.** You may only book a start the customer asked for themselves. If their message does not pin down BOTH a day and an hour, you book nothing this turn: you answer with the real free slots and ask them to reply with the service, the day and the hour. That is not politeness, it is the design — with nobody at the salon to catch it, a bot that picks the hour books people into times they cannot make, and the salon loses the chair and the customer both.

The availability tools you have here only answer questions: they change nothing, they run the moment you call them, and their answers come straight back to you. So ask them first, and act on what they told you.

1. Read the catalogue with `services.services.list` and pick the service they are asking for. If the message is too vague to tell which one, book NOTHING: tell them so in one line and name the services that could fit, so they can pick.
2. Work out how long it takes. If the service declares `duration_minutes`, use it AS IS — the salon decided it. If it is missing or zero, ESTIMATE it from what the service is: a cut is not a colour, and a colour is not a colour with highlights. Be honest, and be generous rather than exact; a booking that falls fifteen minutes short pushes the whole afternoon.
3. Ask `appointments.availability.day_opening` when the salon is open on the date they want. It answers `spans` — minutes from that date's own midnight, with the breaks already carved out — and `source`. If `source` is `schedules` and `spans` is empty, THE SALON IS SHUT that day: book nothing, tell them so, offer the nearest day it is open, and stop. If `source` is `unset` the salon has no rule reaching that date, so nothing is being refused on those grounds and you must not filter by hours yourself.
4. NEVER work the opening hours out on your own, from the message or from anywhere else — and the same goes for the free slots and for who is working. These operations resolve them exactly as the booking gate does — special day, yearly special day, override range, weekly hours, in that order — and a second opinion about when the salon opens is precisely how a booking that looked fine gets refused at the gate.
5. Ask `appointments.availability.slots` for the real free slots on that date for that duration. If they named an hour, confirm THAT hour with `appointments.availability.check`, passing the professional you settled on. If `check` refuses it, do not slide to a different hour on their behalf: take its reason at face value — `outside_schedule` means the salon is shut then, `held` means another request has it set aside for a few minutes — and offer them the free slots around it instead.
6. Use `staff.members.list` and `staff.schedules.list_for_member` to pick a professional who actually works at that hour, and confirm the slot for that person by passing their `staff_id`. Choosing WHO is yours to make; choosing WHEN is not.
7. If the hour they asked for is not free, or they never named one, book NOTHING. Reply with two or three of the real free slots — day, hour and professional by name — and ask them to answer with the service, the day and the hour, spelling out an example: «cut, tomorrow at 10:30». Their next message is a fresh turn that starts from nothing, so it has to carry the service too — an answer of «10:30» on its own reaches you with no idea what it is for. If nothing at all is free that day, say so and offer the nearest day that has room.
8. Resolve the customer with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone` = `+{{input.from}}`.
9. Book it with `appointments.appointments.create`: the customer, the service, the professional, the start you confirmed and `duration_minutes`.

About the duration, this matters: if you ESTIMATED it instead of reading it from the catalogue, say so in `internal_notes`, in words and with the number — for example "Duration estimated by the assistant: 90 min; the catalogue declares none for this service." Nobody approves this booking, so `internal_notes` is where the salon finds out afterwards that the length was a guess and can fix it before the day comes. It is for staff only: the customer never reads it.

Put in `notes` a one-line summary of what the customer asked for, in their own words.

Asking what is free changes nothing. `appointments.appointments.create` is the one call that puts a real appointment in the salon's diary, and it does it immediately: there is no tray, no review, and no way back other than cancelling it.

# CANCELLING

1. Find them with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone` = `+{{input.from}}`. No record means no appointment: tell them there is nothing booked under that number and stop.
2. List what they have with `appointments.appointments.list_for_customer`. It answers newest first and it includes the past and the already-cancelled ones, so take the SOONEST one still to come whose `status` is `pending` or `confirmed`. Anything `cancelled`, `completed` or `no_show` is history — it is not theirs to cancel.
3. If nothing is still to come, tell them there is nothing booked and stop.
4. If more than one is still to come and their message does not say which, cancel NOTHING: NAME them — day, hour and professional — and ask which one. Never guess: cancelling the wrong appointment costs the salon the chair AND the customer. Their answer comes back as a new message and their appointments are still there to be listed, so naming them again is all it takes.
5. Cancel it with `appointments.appointments.cancel`: that `appointment_id`, a `reason` in their own words, `channel` set to `customer`, and the `customer_id` of the person you found in point 1.

That `channel` is not decoration: it is what makes the salon's OWN rules apply — whether customers may cancel at all, and how much notice they owe. And it is why the `customer_id` goes with it: on the customer channel Citas refuses a cancellation that does not say who is asking, and refuses it again if the appointment turns out to belong to somebody else. So it has to be the id you looked up from THEIR phone number in point 1, never one taken from the message or from anywhere else. Citas decides the rest when the cancellation runs, with the settings of this business. Do not work it out yourself, do not tell them it is too late, and do not cancel «anyway»: call it, and if the salon's rules refuse it, tell them exactly what the salon answered.

Never cancel something you have not named to them first.

**And now the part that reaches the customer.** Everything you write back is sent to them on WhatsApp, word for word, as soon as this turn ends — so write it TO them, not about them: their own language, one or two short lines, warm and plain.

- If you booked, tell them what they have: the day, the hour and the professional BY NAME. Never an id, never a tool name, never «pending approval» — by the time they read this, it happened.
- If you cancelled, tell them it is cancelled, naming the appointment you cancelled so they can see it was the right one, and leave the door open to book again.
- If you booked nothing because you need them to choose, give them the free slots and tell them exactly how to answer, with the example.
- If you booked nothing for any other reason, tell them why in one line and offer the nearest alternative, so they can answer with it.
- Never put in here the duration you estimated, what the catalogue did or did not declare, or anything else the salon needs to see. That goes in `internal_notes`, which only the salon reads.

Write it in the SAME reply in which you book: the turn ends when you stop and you will not be asked again, so a booking made with no words leaves them with nothing.

guide.title: How automations work
guide.whatBody: It is a rule you leave written down: when something happens in your business, the hub does something about it — on its own, every time, without anybody having to remember.
guide.whatExample: In a salon: the moment somebody is marked as not having turned up, a job appears on your list telling you to ring them and offer another time. Nobody has to notice. It is already there.
guide.whatCan: It is not only for your own team either: an automation can send your customer a message, ask the assistant to write something, or call another service you use. Those steps are set up on the step itself, inside the automation, like every other one.
guide.firstTitle: Your first automation, step by step
guide.firstBody: The quickest way in is one of the ready-made ones on the first screen.
guide.firstPick: On the Automations screen, pick one from the gallery. Read the sentence underneath: that is exactly what it will do.
guide.firstUse: Press «Use this one». It becomes yours, and it is created switched off.
guide.firstFill: Fill in what it asked you to decide — an amount, a time, how long to wait. It always arrives with a sensible guess in place.
guide.firstAllow: Go to Permissions and allow what it needs. Until you do, it does nothing at all.
guide.firstTest: Press «Try it». It walks the automation against something that really happened in your business and shows you what it WOULD do — without sending, charging or writing anything down.
guide.firstEnable: Now turn it on with the switch at the top. From that moment it is watching, day and night.
guide.permissionsTitle: Permissions: why you have to say yes
guide.permissionsBody: An automation works while you are not looking, so it never borrows your own permissions. It can only do the exact things you allowed it, one by one — that is what stops it from ever doing more than you meant.
guide.permissionsWhere: You allow them inside the automation itself: open it and go to the Permissions tab. Everything it needs is listed there, with one button that allows the lot.
guide.permissionsNothing: An automation you never allowed anything is not broken and it is not slow: it simply does nothing, and it will not complain. If yours has never done a thing, look here first.
guide.historyBody: Open the automation and go to History. Every time it woke up there is a line with the day and the hour, and underneath it, in words, what it did.
guide.historyGuard: «The condition was not met, so it stopped here» is not a fault. That is the automation working: you told it to carry on only in certain cases, and this was not one of them.
guide.limitsBranches: There are no forks. An automation is one line of steps from top to bottom, and that is on purpose: if a condition is not met it stops there — it does not take a second route. Two different outcomes means two automations.
guide.limitsDates: It cannot count backwards from a date: «the day before the appointment» is not something it can work out yet. It can wait a while after something happened, which is not the same thing.
guide.limitsAssistant: And the assistant will not write the message step for you. Ask it for «tell them by message» and it leaves the closest thing it is allowed to propose — the job on your list — and says so in its own notes. Sending a message costs money every time, so that one is yours to add and yours to turn on.
guide.shotGuard: the ticket comes to more than 100,00 €
guide.shotAction: Write a note in the customer's card
guide.shotGrant: Write a note in the customer's card
guide.shotGrantDone: Add a job to your list
